Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2005) * [[California Mr. Basketball]] (2005) }} '''Amir Jalla Johnson''' (born May 1, 1987) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is a player development coach for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Law |date=2024-08-29 |title=Clippers reporter |url=https://x.com/lawmurraythenu/status/1829270617646113112?s=46}} He has previously played for the [[Detroit Pistons]], the team that selected Johnson in the second round of the [[2005 NBA draft]], as well as the [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Boston Celtics]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Los Angeles]], Johnson grew up mainly in [[South Central Los Angeles]], but also spent time as a child in [[Harbor City, Los Angeles|Harbor City]] and [[Watts, Los Angeles|Watts]]. Despite being tall and athletic, Johnson struggled to find a place on a high school basketball team. His freshman year was split at two schools (Pacific Hills, [[Narbonne High School|Narbonne]]), neither of which featured him on the court. From there, he enrolled at [[Verbum Dei High School]], where he enjoyed a solid inaugural season of high school basketball as a sophomore in 2002–03. He then transferred to [[Westchester High School (Los Angeles)|Westchester High School]] but was forced to sit out his junior year of 2003–04. He made up for lost time as a senior in 2004–05 as he was named the 2005 [[California Mr. Basketball]] after leading Westchester to a state title. He was subsequently named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and appeared in the [[2005 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2005 Boys Game]].{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/21548/the-l-a-in-my-game-with-amir-johnson |title="The L.A. in my Game," with Amir Johnson |work=ESPN.com |date=August 18, 2011 |access-date=November 29, 2014}} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Johnson was listed as the No. 7 power forward and the No. 29 player in the nation in 2005.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Amir-Johnson-19387 Amir Johnson – Yahoo! Sports] Despite committing to play for the [[University of Louisville]], Johnson decided to skip college and declared for [[NBA draft]].{{cite news|url=https://www.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=1132&CID=356192 |title=A Look at High School Players in the NBA Draft |work=Rivals.com |access-date=November 29, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205000142/https://www.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=1132&CID=356192 |archive-date=December 5, 2014 }} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2005–2009)=== Johnson was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 56th overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]].[http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/jobtraining_070108.html On-the-Job Training] He is the last [[NBA high school players|direct from high school player]] to be selected in the NBA draft (until 2015 with [[Satnam Singh Bhamara]]), as the NBA instituted a rule prior to the [[2006 NBA draft|2006 draft]] that requires American players to be at least one year removed from the graduation of their high school class to be eligible. As a rookie for the Pistons, Johnson appeared in just three games during the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]]. He scored his first NBA basket on a windmill dunk against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on January 24, 2006. On February 27, 2006, he was assigned to the [[Fayetteville Patriots]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. After appearing in 18 games for the Patriots, he was recalled by the Pistons on April 17, 2006. That same day, he scored 18 points for the Pistons in their 20-point loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], making all six of his [[Field goal (basketball)|field goal]] attempts, both [[three-point field goal|three-point attempts]], and all four of his [[free throw]] attempts.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnsam01/gamelog/2006/ Amir Johnson 2005-06 Game Log] Johnson spent most of the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]] playing for the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the NBA Development League, where he earned Player of the Week honors for his play.[http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/johnson_nbdl_070305.html Amir Johnson Named D-League Performer of the Week] In 22 games for the Skyforce, Johnson averaged 18.9 points, 9.7 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 3.1 blocks per game, while shooting 62.3% from the field.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/nbdl/players/j/johnsam01d.html Amir Johnson D-League Stats] Despite his strong D-League play, Johnson managed just eight games for the Pistons in 2006–07, averaging 5.9 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game. On July 12, 2007, Johnson re-signed with the Pistons to a three-year, $12 million contract.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2934290 |title=Sources: Pistons, forward Johnson agree to 3-year deal |work=ESPN.com |date=July 12, 2007 |access-date=November 29, 2014}} Over the next two seasons, Johnson played a total of 124 games for the Pistons as he became a valuable asset off the bench. He averaged 3.6 points and 3.8 rebounds in 2007–08, and 3.5 points and 3.7 rebounds in 2008–09. He also averaged 1.1 blocks per game over the two seasons.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnsam01.html Amir Johnson NBA & ABA Stats] ===Toronto Raptors (2009–2015)=== On June 23, 2009, Johnson was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in a three three-team trade that also involved the [[San Antonio Spurs]] and [[Richard Jefferson]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks_trade_tracker.html |title=MILWAUKEE BUCKS COMPLETE THREE-TEAM DEAL WITH SAN ANTONIO AND DETROIT |work=NBA.com |date=June 23, 2009 |access-date=June 23, 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090627022123/http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks_trade_tracker.html| archive-date=June 27, 2009 | url-status= live}} He was later traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] on August 18, 2009, along with [[Sonny Weems]], in exchange for [[Carlos Delfino]] and [[Roko Ukić]].{{cite web | title = Raptors Acquire Johnson And Weems From Milwaukee | url = http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/johnson_weems_trade081809.html | work = NBA.com | date = August 18, 2009 | access-date = August 18, 2009}} On July 8, 2010, Johnson re-signed with the Raptors to a five-year, $34 million contract.{{cite web | title = Raptors Re-Sign Free Agent Amir Johnson | url = http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/johnson_re-signs_070810.html | work = NBA.com | date = July 8, 2010 | access-date = November 29, 2014}}{{cite web|last=Koreen |first=Eric |title=Amir Johnson re-signs with Raptors |url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/nba/amir-johnson-re-signs-with-raptors |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141130075608/http://sports.nationalpost.com/2010/07/01/amir-johnson-re-signs-with-raptors/ |url-status=live |archive-date=November 30, 2014 |work=NationalPost.com |date=July 1, 2010 |access-date=November 29, 2014 }} Johnson had a career-best season in 2012–13 as he averaged career-highs in minutes played (28.7 mpg), points (10.0 ppg), rebounds (7.5 rpg), assists (1.5 apg) and steals (1.0 spg). With his continued rise in dominance and overall production, Johnson began to embrace the city of Toronto, quoting that "Toronto is part of me. I've been around, the people are very kind, I love it here."[http://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/raptors-amir-johnson-says-he-s-in-love-with-toronto-1.1895146 Raptors' Amir Johnson says he's in love with Toronto] On December 8, 2013, Johnson scored a career-high 32 points in a 106–94 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.{{cite web | title = Notebook: Raptors 106, Lakers 94 | url = http://www.nba.com/games/20131208/TORLAL/gameinfo.html | work = NBA.com | date = December 8, 2013 | access-date = March 9, 2015}} ===Boston Celtics (2015–2017)=== On July 9, 2015, Johnson signed a two-year, $24 million contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-sign-amir-johnson|title=Boston Celtics Sign Amir points and a season-high 18 rebounds in a 103–94 win over the Indiana Pacers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160113/INDBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Thomas, Celtics snap 4-game skid with 103-94 finished the 2015–16 season with averages of 7.3 points and 6.4 rebounds per game. On November 2, 2016, Johnson scored 23 points and hit a career-high four three-pointers in a 107–100 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899511|title=Thomas, Johnson help lead Celtics past Bulls, 107-100|work=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2016}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2017–2019)=== On July 8, 2017, Johnson signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-sign-veterans-jj-redick-and-amir-johnson|title=Sixers Sign Veterans JJ Redick And Amir Johnson|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2017|access-date=July 8, 2017}} On June 25, 2018, he was named the winner of the [[NBA Hustle Award]] during the [[2018 NBA Awards]].{{cite web |title=Johnson Named Recipient Of 2017-18 NBA Hustle Award |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/johnson-named-recipient-2017-18-nba-hustle-award |website=NBA.com |access-date=June 27, 2018 |date=June 26, 2018}}{{Cite web |title=Sixers veteran big man Amir Johnson wins NBA's Hustle award |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/sixers-veteran-big-man-amir-johnson-wins-nbas-hustle-award |access-date=May 23, 2022 |website=NBC Sports|date=26 June 2018 }} On July 16, 2018, Johnson re-signed with the 76ers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/tickets/team-re-signs-johnson|title=Team Re-Signs Johnson|work=NBA.com|date=July 16, 2018|access-date=July 16, 2018}} On February 22, 2019, he volunteered to play for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] of the [[NBA G League]] because he had not appeared in a game for the 76ers since January 26.{{cite web|last=Todd|first=Sarah|url=https://www.philly.com/sixers/amir-johnson-g-league-sixers-delaware-blue-coats-nba-20190223.html|title=Sixers' Amir Johnson keeps positive spirit by embracing G-League playing time|work=philly.com|date=February 23, 2018|access-date=February 24, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071555|title=Jusuf Nurkic scores 24, Blazers beat Sixers 130-115|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2018|access-date=February 24, 2018}} On April 13, 2019, during a nationally televised playoff game between Philadelphia and the [[Brooklyn Nets]], Johnson was caught by [[ESPN]] cameras sitting on the bench during the game taking a cell phone out of his pocket to show teammate [[Joel Embiid]] a text message, while the Sixers were trailing by ten points. Moments later, Johnson was removed from the bench and returned to the locker room. Johnson was not active for the game.{{Cite web|url=https://thesportsdaily.com/2019/04/13/look-joel-embiid-amir-johnson-caught-checking-cell-phone-during-playoff-game/|title = Look: Joel Embiid, Amir Johnson caught checking cell phone during playoff game|date = 13 April 2019}} At the post game press conference, Embiid stated that Johnson's daughter was very ill and he just looked at the message. After the game, Johnson issued an apology through a statement and was fined an undisclosed amount by the 76ers for violating the NBA's rule against cell phones on the bench. Johnson did not re-sign with the team following the season. ===NBA G League Ignite (2020–2022)=== On November 12, 2020, Johnson was announced as addition to the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/nba-veterans-join-nba-g-league-ignite-to-play-alongside-elite-prospects|title=NBA Veterans Join NBA G League Ignite To Play Alongside Elite Prospects|date=November 12, 2020|website=NBA.com|accessdate=November 12, 2020}} His spot on the roster was confirmed on February 1, 2021.{{cite web|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/nba-g-league-ignite-roster|title=NBA G League Ignite Roster|date=February 1, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=February 1, 2021|archive-date=February 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228034131/https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/nba-g-league-ignite-roster/|url-status=dead}} On October 28, 2021, Johnson re-signed with the Ignite.{{cite web|title=Ignite Announces Veteran Additions, Coaching Staff|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/ignite-announces-veteran-additions-coaching-staff/n-5759170|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}} Johnson did not return to an NBA roster after his time with the Ignite. Thus, his final NBA game was played during Game 6 of the 2019 Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Raptors. The 76ers emptied their bench when they had a 19-point lead with three and a half minutes remaining in the game. This was Johnson's only playing time that game and he grabbed two rebounds as the 76ers won 112 - 101.https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201905090PHI.html Johnson did not play in Game 7 of this series and the 76ers would fall to the Raptors 90 - 92 and be eliminated from the playoffs. ==Coaching career== === NBA G League Ignite (2023–2024) === On October 30, 2023, Johnson was hired as an assistant coach by the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web|title=Ignite Announces Roster For The 2023-24 style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 54 || 25 || 13.9 || .637 || .111 || .654 || 3.5 || .6 || .2 || .5 || 4.9 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Johnson grew up in an athletic family. His sister, Indi, played forward for [[Southern University]]'s women's basketball team, while his cousins, [[Kevin Burnett|Kevin]] and [[Kaelin Burnett]], both played linebacker in the NFL.{{Cite web |url=http://amirjohnson.com/this-is-amir-johnson-the-biography/ |title=This Is Amir Johnson: The Biography |access-date=November 16, 2013 |archive-date=July 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120708111012/http://amirjohnson.com/this-is-amir-johnson-the-biography/ |url-status=dead }} Johnson is highly involved in community work, and regularly hosts back to school programs, visits local hospitals and pays for low income youth to attend games. He is also known for his random acts of kindness. Shortly after the release of [[Drake (rapper)|Drake]]'s ''[[Nothing Was the Same]]'' album, Johnson bought all the copies from two local stores and handed them out to random pedestrians in Toronto. ==See also== * [[List of NBA career field goal percentage leaders]] ==References== {{reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{commons category}} *[https://gleague.nba.com/player/amir-johnson/ NBA G League profile] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20040421025503/http://amirjohnson.com/ Official website] *{{basketball stats|nba=101161|bbr=j/johnsam01}} {{2005 NBA draft}} {{NBA Hustle Award}} {{Portal bar|Sports}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Johnson, Amir}} [[Category:1987 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Canada]] [[Category:American men's 3x3 basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Los Angeles]] [[Category:Big3 players]] [[Category:Boston Celtics players]] [[Category:Delaware Blue Coats players]] [[Category:Detroit Pistons draft picks]] [[Category:Detroit Pistons players]] [[Category:Fayetteville Patriots players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:NBA high school draftees]] [[Category:NBA G League Ignite coaches]] [[Category:NBA G League Ignite players]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:Philadelphia 76ers players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Sioux Falls Skyforce players]] [[Category:Toronto Raptors players]] [[Category:Verbum Dei High School alumni]] [[Category:Westchester High School (Los Angeles) alumni]]
